title: Bioelectric network information cannot be read from transcript or protein levels

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bioelectric network information cannot be read from transcript or protein levels

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because ion channels open and close post-translationally, the same channels can yield different voltage states depending on cell history and different channels can yield the same voltage map, the information content of a bioelectric network cannot be read out at the transcriptional or proteomic level and must be studied in living tissue.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As a corollary, the information content of this network cannot be read out at the transcriptional or even proteomic level: channels open and close post-translationally, and the same channels can give rise to different voltage states depending on cells’ history, while diverse channels can give rise to the exact same voltage map.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Bioelectricity: the ancient cognitive glue”. Scope: Bioelectric networks of neural and non-neural cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Non-uniqueness and predictive insufficiency have explicit tests, and large omics repositories exist. The decisive matched live-tissue datasets are limited, and an absolute claim that information 'cannot' be read out is stronger than finite predictive failures.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Train models to predict live voltage maps from matched transcriptomic or proteomic profiles across tissues and histories, and test identifiability on held-out samples. Demonstrating the same molecular profile with different voltages and different profiles with the same voltage would refute a unique readout.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Matched live voltage and omics measurements are uncommon.

Failure of prediction can reflect measurement limits rather than impossibility.

Bulk omics obscures cell-level states.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Paired gene expression and electrophysiology are public for a large set of neurons and can show how much electrical phenotype is readable from transcripts. That tests the neural subset and can refute an absolute version of unreadability. It does not cover non-neural bioelectric maps, proteomics, or the history dependence the mechanism invokes, so the claim's full scope stays only partly tested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In paired transcriptome and electrophysiology profiles, predict resting or firing features from transcript levels and ask whether distinct channel sets map to the same electrical phenotype. Prediction no better than a permutation null, or identical transcriptomes with different voltage states, would support unreadability; accurate prediction of the electrical phenotype from transcripts or proteins would refute a strict reading.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A snapshot cannot test history dependence, and proteins are not paired with voltage in this resource.

The atlas covers spiking neurons, not the slow developmental voltage patterns the surrounding argument is about.
